card.heard: tokens arrive 50 times a second, how to avoid lag
card.say: I wouldn't update the UI on every chunk. The repository writes chunks into Room, and the UI collects from the database. I'd batch the writes, maybe every 50 to 100 milliseconds, so the screen updates a few times a second, not 50. Compose then only redraws the changed text. The stream itself runs on Dispatchers.IO, never the main thread.

card.heard: AI talking, user starts talking
card.say: I'd stop the AI's speech right away and switch the mic to the user. The voice session runs in a foreground service of type microphone, so it keeps going when the screen is off. I'd also handle audio focus, because a phone call takes it and I have to pause. And I'd use the device's echo cancellation, so the mic doesn't pick up the AI's own voice.

card.say: The call takes audio focus, so I pause the session and stop the AI's speech. I keep the voice session alive in the foreground service, but I don't record while the call is active. Candidate: Out of scope for now: model training and the web client itself.

Candidate: I'll draw the layers now.
Candidate: The data lives in a local database on the phone, and the UI only reads from it.
Candidate: The network layer writes new messages and streamed chunks into that database.
Candidate: So the screen never waits on the network.
[board] Compose UI -> ViewModel -> Repository -> Room DB | Remote API (SSE)

Candidate: So the network never touches the screen directly.
